properties.name: Buttonwillow Safety Roadside Rest Area (northbound)
properties.notes: I-5 northbound, Kern County, 2 mi north of the SR-58 interchange -- about 5 mi from the route's mile-126 I-5 waypoint (35.3733/-119.3617), the first Central Valley I-5 rest stop north of Bakersfield and south of the long Coalinga gap. Restrooms, water, picnic tables, phone, ADA access, vending, pet area per Caltrans; no RV dump. Live Caltrans QuickMap SRRA feed (quickmap.dot.ca.gov/data/srra.kml, checked 2026-08-12) shows this facility status 'Open'. 8-hour/24-hour parking limit, sleeping in vehicle permitted within that limit, camping prohibited (21 CCR 2205(b) parking limit, 2205(a) camping ban). Lighting and typical noise level not stated by Caltrans; open Central Valley truck route -- expect I-5 truck noise, flat terrain, no shade cover noted in the facility record.
properties.source: Caltrans Safety Roadside Rest Areas (GIS) + Caltrans QuickMap live status

properties.name: Crestview Safety Roadside Rest Area
properties.notes: US-395, Mono County, 6.4 mi north of the June Lake Junction (SR-203) -- the closest official CA rest area to Lee Vining on the 395 corridor. Serves both directions. Restrooms, water, picnic tables, phone, ADA access; no RV dump. 8-hour parking limit per 21 CCR 2205(b); sleeping in the vehicle within that limit is permitted, camping is prohibited per 21 CCR 2205(a). High desert, ~7000 ft -- can be cold at night even in summer; not confirmed by source, general route knowledge.

properties.name: John "Chuck" Erreca Safety Roadside Rest Area, Santa Nella (northbound)
properties.notes: I-5 northbound, Merced County, 0.7 mi north of the Fresno county line at Santa Nella -- about 7 mi from the route's mile-250 Los Banos/Santa Nella waypoint (36.7801/-120.7255), and the only official I-5 rest stop between Coalinga and the Stockton/Sacramento area. Restrooms, water, picnic tables, phone, ADA access, vending, pet area per Caltrans; no RV dump. Just finished a ~$30M comfort-station replacement (closed for construction on the southbound side from Apr 2022, reopened 5/5/2026 per Caltrans District 10's own release, which also states the rebuild added EV charging capacity) -- both directions confirmed 'Open' on the live Caltrans QuickMap SRRA feed checked 2026-08-12. 8-hour/24-hour parking limit, sleeping in vehicle permitted within that limit, camping prohibited (21 CCR 2205(b), 2205(a)). Lighting/noise not stated by Caltrans; I-5/CA-152 junction area, expect truck and highway noise, flat open Central Valley setting.
properties.source: Caltrans Safety Roadside Rest Areas (GIS) + Caltrans QuickMap live status

properties.name: John "Chuck" Erreca Safety Roadside Rest Area, Santa Nella (southbound)
properties.notes: I-5 southbound counterpart at Santa Nella, Merced County. Restrooms, water, picnic tables, phone, ADA access, vending, pet area per Caltrans; no RV dump. This was the side under long-term closure (Apr 2022 - 5/5/2026) for the comfort-station rebuild noted on the northbound record; Caltrans District 10 announced the reopening and the live QuickMap SRRA feed (checked 2026-08-12) confirms status 'Open' for both directions now, with added EV charging capacity from the rebuild. 8-hour/24-hour parking limit, sleeping in vehicle permitted within that limit, camping prohibited (21 CCR 2205(b), 2205(a)). Lighting/noise not stated by source.
properties.source: Caltrans Safety Roadside Rest Areas (GIS) + Caltrans QuickMap live status

properties.name: Wadsworth Rest Area (I-80 westbound, mile marker ~42-43)
properties.notes: Location and mile marker from camping.org and nevadarestareas.com (secondary/user-report aggregators), not NDOT's own site -- dot.nv.gov blocked automated fetch (403) and its Wayback snapshot had no usable content. Westbound-access-only, I-80 near Wadsworth, the last formal rest stop before the climb into Reno on this corridor. Overnight-policy reports directly conflict between sources: one summary (citing NDOT generally) states an 18-hour limit within any 2-week period with sleeping in the vehicle permitted; a different rest-area review site states a flat 24-hour limit with 'no overnight parking and no overnight camping,' napping only. Could not independently confirm either against an official NDOT source -- verify posted signage on arrival, do not assume either rule holds.
